neighbours.label: the verb 'cloned' / 'clone' (copying a person, animal or thing), as against other verbs of making or copying
fire: In 1996 a team in Scotland cloned a sheep from a single adult cell.
My manager must have cloned himself, since he attends every meeting at once.
Before editing anything, she cloned the repository onto her laptop.
The company cloned the popular game and sold it under a new name.
Researchers later cloned the gene and inserted it into yeast cells.
The gardener cloned the rare rose by taking cuttings from the old bush.
Thieves had cloned his bank card and emptied the account overnight.
A lab in Korea claimed it had cloned a dog for a grieving owner.
quiet: In 1996 a team in Scotland bred a sheep from a rare mountain flock.
My manager must have doubled his hours, since he attends every meeting at once.
Before editing anything, she downloaded the files onto her laptop.
The company copied the popular game and sold it under a new name.
Researchers later found the gene and studied it in yeast cells.
The gardener grew the rare rose by planting seeds from the old bush.
Thieves had stolen his bank card and emptied the account overnight.
A lab in Korea claimed it had trained a dog for a grieving owner.

notes: Card peaks are scattered (' cloned' x2, ' to', ' of', ' video', ' poster', ' weekend', 'music'). Probe: 'has cloned herself' 0.545, 'The Catholic bishops' 0.201, 'poster child' 0.002, 'weekend warriors' 0.049. Only 'cloned' was strong, so the test is the bare word in varied contexts; low confidence that it generalises.
